solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Late show of hesitation during calls for doubles

parts.note: a late person is a dead one

indicators.note: one piece sits within the span of the other, so it goes inside

parts.note: rings are telephone calls
er is the sound people make when hesitating

explanation.surface: A late-night show where someone hesitates while phoning in to ask about doubles.
explanation.definitionFit: Dead ringers are people who look exactly alike, so doubles of one another.

clue.text: Slow copper left journalist with such cheeks

parts.note: dim means slow-witted
p is a penny, a copper coin
ed is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A slow police officer leaves a journalist with a cheeky look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' suggests a policeman but is a penny, P.
explanation.definitionFit: Dimpled describes cheeks with small hollows that show when smiling.

clue.text: Appropriate name in a divorcee

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name
an ex is a former spouse, such as a divorcee

explanation.surface: A suitable name for a divorced person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' looks like an adjective (suitable) but is the verb, to take over; 'in a' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To annex territory is to seize or appropriate it.

clue.text: Just ego is hurt — badly

indicators.note: badly signals the letters are put together poorly, in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone's pride is just badly wounded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' looks like 'only', but it is the adjective meaning fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Just and righteous both mean morally upright and fair.

clue.text: Never run-of-the-mill, except for the first half

indicators.note: the first half of the word is removed, leaving only its second half

parts.note: ordinary means run-of-the-mill, unremarkable

explanation.surface: Never ordinary, apart from the first half of something.
explanation.walkthrough: ORDINARY has eight letters; dropping the first four leaves the second half.
explanation.definitionFit: Nary is a dialect word meaning not one, so never, as in nary a word.

clue.text: Small hole on ship is what attracts attention to viewer

indicators.note: in a down clue, on puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: an eye is a small hole, as in a needle
a liner is a passenger ship

explanation.surface: A porthole on a ship draws the eye of an onlooker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'viewer' is the eye itself, which the make-up highlights.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyeliner is make-up that outlines and draws attention to the eye.

clue.text: Name of star oddly featuring in tabloid

indicators.note: featuring in means appearing within, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper

indicators.note: oddly picks the first, third and other odd-placed letters

explanation.surface: A star's name appears in a tabloid newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The odd letters of STAR are S and A; these go into SUN, the British tabloid.
explanation.definitionFit: Susan is a common female first name.

clue.text: Preschool carer — really heartless

parts.note: a nurse is a carer for the sick

indicators.note: heartless removes the middle of the word, leaving its outer letters

explanation.surface: A preschool carer is really cruel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' suggests cruelty but removes the middle of REALLY, leaving RY.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursery is a school for very young children before primary age.

clue.text: Charming fellow making a deep impression

parts.note: an etching is a print made from deeply incised lines

explanation.surface: A charming man makes a strong impression.
explanation.definitionFit: Fetching means attractive or charming.

clue.text: Various animals emerge in a novel?

indicators.note: novel means new or fresh, so the preceding letters take a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A collection of animals appears in a work of fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book in which animals emerge, but it is the anagram signal working on EMERGE IN A.
explanation.definitionFit: A menagerie is a collection of assorted wild animals kept for show.

clue.text: The girl with a red top or fleece

parts.note: she is the pronoun for a girl

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A girl with a red top, or a fleece jacket, as a clothing choice.
explanation.definitionFit: To fleece a sheep is to cut off its wool, which is shearing it.

clue.text: Permissiveness of times shown in non-church people

indicators.note: one piece is displayed inside the other, so it goes within

parts.note: the laity are people who are not clergy
x is the multiplication sign, read as times

explanation.surface: Ordinary churchgoers are said to show the lax attitudes of the age.
explanation.definitionFit: Laxity is slackness in standards, a tolerant permissiveness.

clue.text: Peak Practice's opening leads to popular, clean broadcast

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: Seems to describe the TV drama Peak Practice leading to a popular, family-friendly show.
explanation.walkthrough: Peak Practice was a British TV medical drama; here 'Peak' is the definition and 'Practice's opening' gives P.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinnacle is the highest point, a summit or peak.

clue.text: Drake losing heart — trick is to spread out

indicators.note: the middle of the word goes, leaving just its outside letters

parts.note: a ploy is a cunning trick

explanation.surface: Sir Francis Drake, dispirited, plans a trick to scatter his forces.
explanation.definitionFit: To deploy troops is to spread them out into position.

clue.text: Implements choice on cuts

indicators.note: in a down clue, on puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: pick means choice, as in take your pick
axes means cuts, as in budget cuts

explanation.surface: Seems to say a choice is made about budget cuts to be implemented.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Implements' looks like a verb but is the noun, tools.
explanation.definitionFit: Pickaxes are digging tools, which are implements.

clue.text: Past life changed, without a year for a feeling such as this

indicators.note: changed means altered, so the letters are rearranged
without means lacking, so the next letter is taken out

explanation.surface: Someone regrets a past life that has changed, a year on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes the A from PAST LIFE, leaving PSTLIFE; add Y and rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-pity is the sorry feeling of dwelling on one's own past misfortunes.

clue.text: Could one throw light on future developments?

definitions.text: Could one throw light on future developments?

parts.words: Could one throw light on future developments?
parts.note: a camera ... lit scenes for photos later developed, not a prediction of the future

explanation.surface: Asks whether something might illuminate what is coming next.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developments' sounds like future events, but it is photographic film being developed.
explanation.definitionFit: A flash bulb gave a burst of light for a photograph, whose film was then developed.

clue.text: Friendliness of posh bloke up before one in residence

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word reads from the bottom

parts.note: a nob is an upper-class person

indicators.note: in places one letter within the other word

parts.note: home is a residence
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: The friendliness of an upper-class man coming before someone at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonhomie is cheerful friendliness and good nature.

clue.text: Rabbit's spicy, having been peppered with this?

parts.note: a buck is a male rabbit, here with the possessive s
hot means spicy, as in a curry

explanation.surface: A rabbit has a spicy flavour after being peppered with lead shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peppered' looks like seasoning to go with 'spicy', but it means riddled with shot.
explanation.definitionFit: Buckshot is the coarse lead shot that peppers a target when fired from a shotgun.

clue.text: Rich people supporting live acts

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting puts the second piece beneath the first

parts.note: be means exist or live
the haves are the wealthy, as in haves and have-nots

explanation.surface: Wealthy people back live performances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'live acts' looks like shows, but 'live' gives BE and 'acts' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Behaves and acts both mean conducts oneself.

clue.text: Golf — after mother fetched grub

indicators.note: after places the golf letter following the word for mother

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet
got means fetched, as in went and got

explanation.surface: After a round of golf, mother went off to get some food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grub' looks like slang for food, matching the surface, but here it means a larva.
explanation.definitionFit: A maggot is a fly larva, which is a kind of grub.

clue.text: Still worried about engineers providing a framework for growth

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes inside the other
worried means agitated, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: Engineers remain anxious about building a structure for growth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like an adverb or a quiet state, but it is the anagram fodder; the setting is a garden structure for climbing plants.
explanation.definitionFit: A trellis is a lattice framework that supports climbing plants as they grow.

clue.text: Boss of kitchen sacking female over a problem

indicators.note: over here means placed across or around, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a head is a boss or leader

indicators.note: sacking means firing, so the letter is removed

parts.note: a chef works in and runs a kitchen

explanation.surface: The head chef has trouble after firing a woman from the kitchen staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss of kitchen' reads as one title, head chef, but splits into two pieces; 'sacking' drops the female letter and 'over' wraps the result around A.
explanation.definitionFit: A headache is a figurative trouble or problem.

clue.text: Agree to get rid of new item of value

indicators.note: get rid of means discard, so the letter is removed

parts.note: assent means agree

explanation.surface: Agreeing to dispose of a new valuable item.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is a valuable possession or resource.

clue.text: A few words from Romeo, in poor shape

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
poor means in bad condition, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: R is Romeo in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Romeo, the lover, offers a few words while in poor condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor shape' makes PHASE, the anagram of SHAPE, and R goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase is a short group of words.

clue.text: So long a day that is universal

parts.note: ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is
U is the film certificate for universal

explanation.surface: Such a long day that it seems universal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'So long' looks like a measure of time, but it is a farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu and so long are both ways of saying goodbye.

clue.text: Amount charged about right for release

indicators.note: about means around, so the first piece encloses the second

parts.note: a fee is an amount charged

explanation.surface: A fee is charged for someone's release.
explanation.definitionFit: To free someone is to release them.

clue.text: Struggles to take in Western perspectives

indicators.note: take in means to contain, so the second piece goes inside

parts.note: vies means competes or struggles

explanation.surface: Someone struggles to accept Western outlooks.
explanation.definitionFit: Views are opinions or points of view, that is, perspectives.

clue.text: Creature from another planet leading one with a line

parts.note: Mars is a planet other than our own
up means ahead or leading, as in a match
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An alien from another planet arrives at the front, carrying a line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Creature from another planet' looks like a single phrase for an alien; the definition is just 'Creature'.
explanation.definitionFit: A marsupial is a pouched mammal such as a kangaroo, so a creature.

clue.text: Saboteur worried by article nearby

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: worried means agitated, so the letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A saboteur is troubled by a newspaper article about something close at hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Thereabouts means near that place, in the vicinity.
